title: Expressions, hygienic macros and C interoperability
outcome: Inspect syntax without evaluating untrusted text, implement a hygienic single-evaluation macro and call a precisely typed Linux C function.

exercises.title: Inspect syntax
exercises.task: Identify the head and first argument of parsed 1+2.
exercises.expected: The head is:call and the function symbol is:+.
exercises.answer: The representation describes a call; this inspection does not evaluate arbitrary input.

exercises.title: Detect duplicate evaluation
exercises.task: Explain what the counter would show if the macro evaluated its argument twice.
exercises.answer: The test protects against duplicated side effects in generated syntax.

exercises.title: Check name ownership
exercises.task: Explain why the caller result variable stays 99.
exercises.hint: Only the caller expression is escaped.
exercises.answer: Generated temporary names must not capture unrelated caller bindings.

exercises.title: Trace UTF 8 bytes
exercises.task: Compare strlen and length for the accented character.
exercises.expected: The byte count is 2 and character count is 1.
exercises.hint: The C API operates on bytes.
exercises.answer: Unicode text has multiple valid units; choose the unit required by the interface.

exercises.title: Reject embedded zeros
exercises.task: Explain why the wrapper rejects a zero byte inside a string.
exercises.expected: C strlen would stop at the first zero.
exercises.hint: The complete-string contract would be violated.
exercises.answer: Explicit validation prevents a truncated prefix from being mistaken for the full length.

exercises.title: Review a native API
exercises.task: List the extra facts needed before calling a function that stores a pointer.
exercises.expected: ABI, lifetime, ownership, thread safety and release rules.
exercises.hint: The argument must outlive the native use.
exercises.answer: A successful synchronous call does not establish a safe retained-pointer integration.
